same_medians_basis: extract_t1_prices is the same function in both files (script lines 327-344, lambda lines 185-202: same filter expressions, same MAX_UNIT_PRICE value, same groupby and median) and both are fed by the same load_transactions_for_date (same key, same trade_date coercion, no dedupe). So the median is computed ONCE and compared once. What differs is only which assets then take that median as their served price (see the two 'serves' cells: the script lets overrides and Yahoo outrank it; the Lambda lets it outrank Yahoo).

medians.precision: 8 decimal places: the price is compared after round(8), the precision the paths' own daily price file normalises to (save_daily_prices_trigger, script line 635 and lambda line 467)
medians.dedupe_rule: drop_duplicates(subset=['transaction_id'], keep='last') on the whole day frame, before the path's own filters: the rule the same files already use on their history route (script lines 258-259, lambda lines 136-137). A keep='first' run gave the same counts.
medians.reading: Of the 160 per-asset medians the day object yields, 151 are taken over rows where at least one transaction id appears more than once; 34 of the 160 differ once each id is counted once (26 by under 0.1 percent, 6 by 0.1 to 1 percent, 2 by more than 1 percent). Every repeated priced id carries one and the same per-row price in all its copies, so the movement comes only from the weight, as ORIGINAL_STORE_SHAPE.json predicted.

does_the_served_price_move.lambda_path: yes, for the medians that moved: every asset with a priced row takes its median as the served price (T1 outranks Yahoo there), so the 34 moved medians are 34 served-price candidates for that day. Whether each is the price that landed in canonical_prices on that day was not read (canonical_prices.parquet is outside this order's one read).
does_the_served_price_move.script_path: only for the assets with no scoped override and no Yahoo close, which was not computed (ticker_lookup.json and historical_prices.parquet are outside this order's one read), so the number of served script prices that move is NOT_ESTABLISHED, between 0 and 34.
does_the_served_price_move.is_the_deduped_price_the_right_one: not judged. This cell shows the median moves; it does not show which weighting is correct for a price. The history route of the same files counts each id once; the per-date route counts it once per portfolio group copy.
